newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ shares finish slightly higher on book squaring.
newsitem.headline: NZ shares finish slightly higher on book squaring.

text.p: * New Zealand sharemarket ends short session up marginally
* Flurry of Telecom buying at close met by sellers
* Brokers cite book-squaring for solid turnover
Price movements at close
LAST CHG
321 -3 * NZSC cap index +31.93 at 5,078.32
339 -3 * Volume NZ$36.8 million. Futures untraded
722 +4 * Other movers - +25 -10
New Zealand shares ended a shortened pre-holiday session at noon on Tuesday marginally higher as brokers squared their books ahead of the New Year break.
The NZSE capital index ended 1996 up 3.21 points at 2,359.64.
The market opens again for a full day's trading on Friday.
Derek Howarth, a trader with Christchurch brokerage Lawrence Milton Howarth, said there was support for Telecom at the close at NZ$7.22.
"But it was met with equally heavy selling, and it was a relief they ended four cents up," he said.
"Tranzrail surprised a little jumping 20 cents to $8.60 after closing at $8.32 in New York," Howarth said.

"I think there was a lot of end-of-year squaring of books. If you have orders on your books you don't leave them over New Year because there is always a fear Wall St will have a correction. Earlier in the week there was talk Wall St would have this 'Santa Claus' rally until the New Year but it was very divided where it would go from there."
He said there was some buying of high-yielding stocks such as Cavalier, up five cents, and Telecom.
